types.name: Letter shift
types.description: A word is coded as another letter group of the same length where each letter moves forward or backward in the alphabet (CAT → DBU, FACED → GZDDE), including "how is the code itself coded" or decoding a code back to the word.

types.name: Opposite letters
types.description: Each letter is replaced by its opposite letter from the other end of the alphabet (A ↔ Z, B ↔ Y, GOLD → TLOW), sometimes with the order also reversed.

types.name: Rearranged letters
types.description: The code uses the same letters (or the same letters shifted) in a new order: reversed, pairs swapped, halves reversed (GARDEN → NEDRAG, CREATION → RCAEITNO).

types.name: Letters to numbers
types.description: A word is coded as a number or a string of numbers (PAINT = 80, BAD = 214, LAMINATE = 121139141205) using letter positions, their sum, product or reverse positions.

types.name: Sentence codes
types.description: Several sentences or phrases are given with codes ('tea is hot' = 'ka la ma', or 'come home soon' = '444'); find the code of a word or a new phrase by comparing common words or counting letters.

types.name: Substitution
types.description: One word is "called" another word ('sky' is called 'cloud', 'cloud' is called 'water' …); asks what something is called in that language.
